name: Generalised Vaidya Spacetime
description: Prahlad Chunilal Vaidya's metric with the mass inside each sphere depending on the radius as well as on null time, so that null dust streams through a fluid whose density and pressures follow from the mass function. Viqar Husain found the first family in 1996, with pressure in proportion to density, Edward N. Glass and Jean P. Krisch gave the outgoing form with a fluid of strings in 1998, and Anzhong Wang and Yumei Wu showed in 1999 that the matter is linear in the mass function, so solutions add.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and every mass is written as a length, $G/c^2$ times the mass. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
The mass inside each sphere of Prahlad Chunilal Vaidya's metric changes with time alone, as null dust streams through, energy moving along light rays with no pressure [vaidya1951, husain1996null, wang1999generalized]. Viqar Husain, at Pennsylvania State University, let that mass depend on the areal radius $r$ as well as on the advanced time $v$, the time that is constant along ingoing light rays, $$ds^2 = -\left(1 -  rac{2m(v, r)}{r}ight)dv^2 + 2\,dv\,dr + r^2d\Omega^2,$$ in units with $G = c = 1$, and published the solutions in February 1996 [husain1996null]. Husain read the matter off the metric first, an energy density $ho$ and a pressure $P$ around each sphere, and then imposed $P = kho$ with $k$ a constant [husain1996null]. The mass function then obeys an equation linear in $m$, solved for $k 
eq 1/2$ by $m = f(v) - g(v)/\left((2k - 1)r^{2k - 1}ight)$ with $f$ and $g$ any two functions of the advanced time [husain1996null]. With $g = 0$ it is Vaidya's metric, and with $k = 1$ it is the charged Vaidya metric, whose static form, $f = M$ and $2g = Q^2$, is Reissner-Nordström's [husain1996null].¶For $k > 1/2$ the spacetime is flat far from the centre, and for $k < 1/2$ it is cosmological [husain1996null]. Husain followed electromagnetic radiation, $k = 1/3$, collapsing from flat space to a black hole, and a family at $k = 1$ in which a naked singularity becomes a black hole that forms at a finite mass [husain1996null]. For $1/2 < k < 1$ the black holes left at late times have hair, and in Husain's words they "fall between" the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström metrics [husain1996null]. J. David Brown and Husain wrote down in 1997 the static black holes these collapses settle into, with $1 - 2M/r + Q^{2k}/r^{2k}$ in place of $1 - 2m/r$ and matter whose pressure along the radius is minus its energy density [brown1997hair]. For $k > 1$ the charge $Q$ falls off too fast for a surface integral at spatial infinity to measure it, so it is hair, and with $k$ as large as one likes the hair can be arbitrarily short [brown1997hair]. The collapsing metric, Brown and Husain wrote, "is to the short hair black hole what the Vaidya metric is to the Schwarzschild black hole" [brown1997hair].¶Edward N. Glass and Jean P. Krisch, at the University of Michigan, let the mass depend on the radius in Vaidya's outgoing metric in 1998, written in the retarded time $u$, and found two fluids outside the star, the outgoing light and a fluid of strings [glass1998string]. The strings stretch along the radius with a tension equal to their density, and Glass and Krisch let them diffuse to find exact solutions in closed form [glass1998string, glass1999twofluid]. In their models the strings diffuse inward while the light streams outward, and the star loses its mass more slowly than it would by the outgoing light alone [glass1999twofluid]. Anzhong Wang and Yumei Wu, in Rio de Janeiro, wrote the ingoing and outgoing forms together, with $\epsilon = \pm 1$ multiplying $2\,dv\,dr$, in a letter of 1999 titled "Generalized Vaidya Solutions" [wang1999generalized]. The densities and pressures of the matter are linear in the mass function, as Wang and Wu observed, so the sum of two solutions is a solution [wang1999generalized]. Expanding $m$ in powers of $r$, they found the field of a monopole in the term $ar/2$, de Sitter or anti-de Sitter space in $\Lambda r^3/6$, the charged Vaidya metric in $f(v) - q^2(v)/2r$, and Husain's solutions, and their sum, in their words, "would represent the monopole-de Sitter-charged Vaidya solutions" [wang1999generalized].¶The matter is null dust streaming along the light rays of constant $v$, with an energy density proportional to $\partial m/\partial v$, alongside a fluid with $ho \propto \partial m/\partial r$ and $P \propto -\partial^2m/\partial r^2$ [wang1999generalized]. Wang and Wu classed the whole as a type II fluid, one with a double null eigenvector [wang1999generalized]. With $m$ a function of $r$ alone the null dust is absent and the fluid is of type I [wang1999generalized]. Glass and Krisch found $\Psi_2$ to be the only Weyl scalar that does not vanish, so the spacetime is of Petrov type D wherever $\Psi_2 
eq 0$ [glass1999twofluid]. Yaghoub Heydarzade and Farhad Darabi let the two constants of Valery Kiselev's black hole of 2003, surrounded by quintessence, change with time in 2018, and Husain's solutions are the case with Kiselev's state parameter $w = (2k - 1)/3$ [heydarzade2018surrounded, kiselev2003].¶Husain concluded that "All of the new solutions support the cosmic censorship conjecture" [husain1996null]. Tiberiu Harko and Kwongsang Cheng added strange quark matter, with the bag model's equation of state, to the infalling light in 2000, and found the central singularity naked for some choices of the free functions [harko2000quark]. Sushant G. Ghosh and Naresh Dadhich took that collapse to higher dimensions in 2002, where the quark matter shrinks the set of initial data that end in a naked singularity [ghosh2002typeii]. Sunil Maharaj, Gabriel Govender, and Megandhren Govender matched a heat conducting star to a generalised Vaidya exterior in 2012, and found the pressure at its surface set by the heat flux inside and the density of the strings outside [maharaj2012atmospheres]. Maombi Mkenyeleye, Rituparno Goswami, and Maharaj worked out in 2014 the conditions on a general mass function under which the collapse ends in a naked central singularity, found such singularities strong, and found them for mass functions of Husain's form too [mkenyeleye2014].¶Martin Bojowald, Goswami, Roy Maartens, and Parampreet Singh put a generalised Vaidya exterior in 2005 around a collapsing scalar field with the corrections of loop quantum gravity, which replace the singularity with a bounce, and found that below a threshold mass no horizon forms [bojowald2005threshold]. Vitalii Vertogradov proved in 2025 that a regular black hole that evaporates in a generalised Vaidya spacetime ends as an object with no horizon and a regular centre [vertogradov2025horizon]. Soumya Chakrabarti, Dadhich, and Chiranjeeb Singha proved in 2026 that a region with $\partial m/\partial r 
eq 0$ cannot be joined smoothly to a Schwarzschild or Vaidya exterior across a finite boundary, where a thin shell of matter appears [chakrabarti2026limitations]. They read the spacetime as "an unbounded geometry with intrinsic heat flux" [chakrabarti2026limitations]. Vertogradov and Ali Övgün found in 2026 that in a self similar collapse the shadow of Husain's black hole is larger than Vaidya's for $0 \le k < 1/2$ and smaller for $1/2 < k \le 1$ [vertogradov2026shadow].

related.text: Vaidya's metric is the case where the mass depends on null time alone. Then the fluid is gone and only the null dust streams through [wang1999generalized].
The charged member, with $m = f(v) - q^2(v)/2r$, whose fluid is the electric field of the charge $q$. It is Husain's family at $k = 1$ [husain1996null, wang1999generalized].

Valery Kiselev's static black hole is Husain's family with $f$ and $g$ held constant and $w = (2k - 1)/3$. Yaghoub Heydarzade and Farhad Darabi let its two constants change with time [heydarzade2018surrounded].
Husain's family at $k = 1$ with $f = M$ and $2g = Q^2$ held constant, the static charged black hole [husain1996null].
Kottler's black hole is the static case $m = M + \Lambda r^3/6$, a mass and a cosmological constant added together [wang1999generalized].

The global monopole is the static case $m = r_s/2 + \Delta r/2$, with $\Delta$ the solid angle deficit. Anzhong Wang and Yumei Wu identified the term linear in $r$ with the field of a monopole [wang1999generalized].
Ronald Mallett's star is the outgoing case $m = m(u) + \Lambda r^3/6$, Vaidya's light and a cosmological constant added together [wang1999generalized].

Sean Hayward's black hole is the case $m = Mr^3/(r^3 + 2M\ell^2)$, with $\ell$ the length of its de Sitter core. Hayward let $M$ change with null time so that the hole forms and evaporates [hayward2006, mkenyeleye2014].
Vaidya's ingoing light in anti-de Sitter space. In four dimensions it is the case $m = m(v) + \Lambda r^3/6$ with $\Lambda < 0$ [wang1999generalized].

parameters.description: Mass function, a length: $G/c^2$ times the mass inside the sphere of radius $r$ at the advanced time $v$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v$ having dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cv$, where $\partial_v m$ means $c^{-1}\partial m/\partial v$, and $\dot{v}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(cv)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{32r^2\left(\partial_r m\right)^2 - 16r^3\,\partial_r m\,\partial_r^2 m - 64m\,r\,\partial_r m + 4r^4\left(\partial_r^2 m\right)^2 + 16m\,r^2\,\partial_r^2 m + 48m^2}{r^6}

coordinates.name: Husain's Null Fluid

parameters.description: Ratio of the pressure $P$ around each sphere to the energy density $\rho$ of the fluid, $P = k\rho$, a pure number with $k \neq 1/2$
Function of the advanced time, a length: the part of the mass function that does not depend on $r$
Function of the advanced time, a length, which sets the fluid's energy density, $\rho = \left(c^4/4\pi Gr^2\right)\left(q/r\right)^{2k}$
The fluid's term in the lapse, a pure number
Mass function, a length, the solution of $P = k\rho$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v$ having dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius, and take components in the chart $x^0 = cv$. Husain's function $g$ is written $q^{2k}$, with $q$ a length. A prime is a derivative along $x^0$, $f' = df/d(cv)$, and $\dot{v}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(cv)/d\lambda$.
